factors: Four-page original author announcement plus a 2,200-word Reader with seven mapped claims
Separately sourced formal verification, mathematical interpretation and collaboration provenance limitations
complexity.rationale: A detailed Reader with seven mapped claims and explicitly scoped technical evidence is sufficient; it does not purport to audit a 14-part mathematical proof or launch an engineering change.

sourceMap.rationale: The author announcement supports only first-person claims about discovery and model contributions, not independent provenance of each insight.
The original formal-proof claim is distinguished from MIT independent checker reports, exact target comparison and the Robin/Lagarias arithmetic cross-check.
The original claim is compared against still-running checks and Clay institutional status without misrepresenting either as a formal proof rejection.

sourceCoverage.rationale: The author original note, MIT verification record, Nature reporting and Clay institutional sources are identified separately, with private original-note digest and three exact source-locator sections.

supportingArgument.rationale: The article follows the author claim through the Lean module build, axioms, independent kernels, statement comparator and arithmetic cross-check, preserving the still-running end-to-end tests.

evidenceRoles.rationale: The author testimony, MIT checker outputs, Nature interpretation and Clay institutional status have distinct evidentiary roles; GhostMesh did not run a proof checker.

counterargument.rationale: Andrew Granville questioned whether the write-up could be assessed; this limitation is not exaggerated into a mathematical counterexample, and Clay status is not presented as kernel rejection.

tradeoffs.rationale: The investigation separates mechanized proof acceptance from mathematical intelligibility, chain-of-custody risk, human review effort and attribution of machine-generated discoveries.

falsifiability.rationale: The exact theorem definitions, axioms, checker implementations, imported libraries and outstanding lake-comparator runs provide explicit ways new evidence could strengthen or undermine the claim.

originalSynthesis.rationale: The operating lesson is that validated proof objects, mathematical understanding, attribution and institutional authority are separate stages that deserve separate accountable evidence records.

performance.rationale: Module and declaration counts are reported only from MIT technical checks, without inventing GhostMesh execution or general AI productivity benchmarks.

economics.rationale: The essay does not claim computational cost savings or value metrics from a formal proof. It identifies any economic implications as outside independently measured evidence.

threatGovernance.rationale: The article treats software trust, statement alignment, source provenance, accepted axioms and reviewer authority as distinct assurance boundaries, avoiding claims of universal AI autonomy.

ownerDecision.approval: Check Pale Horse and the threads. There is one defect you need to fix. Go check Slack.

gaps.rationale: Pale Horse exact-head visual and Slack provenance review not yet returned for this CSS-only repair; prior accepted mathematical and artwork content is unchanged.

decisionRationale: Tony identified the simultaneous sun/moon display in the Reader 71 theme control and directed segfault to fix the defect. The implementation is CSS-only within the existing authored article. Peer acceptance of the current correction is pending; original verified mathematical and image content stays unchanged.
